readme.badge_anchor_form_note: Every that wraps a badge must open, contain the img, and close on ONE line. A newline plus indent inside the anchor is link TEXT, and GitHub renders it as an underlined gap between badges. Readability is not a reason to reformat it back.
readme.header_emoji_note: No emoji above the first '## ' heading — that region is the banner, badge rows, H1 and tagline. Body prose below the first '##' is unrestricted.

banner.note: A hero banner is a designed graphic with a motif drawn from the project's domain, not a wordmark on a rectangle. The numbers are the observable floor enforced by scripts/check-readme-branding.sh; the art direction is the reference above.

feature_equivalence.capability_registry_note: The registry is the single source of truth for the platform set and every capability status. feature-equivalence.json carries only the artifact delta; platform-targets.json carries only versions plus a derived capability mirror. check-feature-equivalence.sh fails when any of the three disagree.

offline_scoring._comment: Every S4 id below needs the GitHub API. score-standards-gaps.sh already refuses to emit them when CONTRACT_OFFLINE=1 or when branch_governance.readable is false; this list is the second gate, applied by score-contract-gaps.sh, so a vendored or older scorer still stays quiet offline. S4-03 is retired — it required at least one approving review, which contradicts the canonical policy and the live repository (0 required approvals with review-thread resolution ON, the solo-contributor posture). Its id is kept here so any un-updated copy of the scorer remains silent rather than failing an offline gate.

retired_check_ids.S4-03: Retired 2026-08-19. Required >= 1 approving review; the approving-review count is policy content owned by config/github/repository-policy.json, and the canonical value is 0 with required_review_thread_resolution true. Superseded by S4-10.
retired_check_ids.S4-04: Retired 2026-08-19. Required allow_auto_merge on every repository. Auto-merge is a team-norm PREFERENCE, not a defect when absent — the same class of error as S4-03: a posture asserted as a universal good. Nothing observable distinguishes a repo that has deliberately left auto-merge off from one that forgot, so no gap can be scored honestly. pr-dev already resolves auto-merge per repository at delivery time (resolve-merge-policy.sh, precedence: TAMIRS_AUTO_MERGE > objective.json > .dev-files/policy.json > repository capability), which is where the preference belongs. S4-05 (delete_branch_on_merge) is retained: it is hygiene with no counter-argument.
